proposal.title: IBM log/trace incident analysis – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic logs and OpenTelemetry traces are collected, redacted, indexed with trace IDs, and analysed by a watsonx.ai-backed runtime that returns an evidence-cited incident explanation to an operator. Assumptions: region not selected, IBM account and model access not verified, no native generator coverage for these IBM services yet (engineering required). Log text is treated as untrusted data and never as instructions.

data.label: Synthetic services (logs + traces)
data.description: Existing synthetic workload emitting JSON logs and OpenTelemetry spans with shared trace IDs. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Collection
data.description: Receives logs and OTLP traces, normalises fields (timestamp, service, trace_id, span_id) and forwards to redaction. Batch and retry with bounded buffer.
data.service: IBM Cloud Logs Routing + OpenTelemetry Collector on Code Engine

data.label: Redaction
data.description: Masks secrets, tokens, emails and IPs before storage; records redaction counts. Original unredacted data is not retained.

data.label: Log & trace search
data.description: Indexes redacted log events and spans by time window, service and trace_id for correlation queries. Retention to be agreed.

data.label: Redacted archive
data.description: Immutable copy of redacted batches for replay, evaluation and audit.

data.label: Incident analysis runtime
data.description: Takes an operator question, queries correlated logs/spans, wraps evidence as quoted untrusted data, calls the model, validates that every claim cites an evidence ID, and abstains when evidence is insufficient. Returns the explanation with source evidence.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Generates the incident explanation from supplied evidence only. Model choice, regional availability and entitlement not yet verified. Mocked in local tests.

data.label: Incident operator
data.description: Person asking about an incident and reviewing the cited explanation. Authenticated via IBM Cloud IAM / App ID (to be decided).

data.label: Audit & monitoring
data.description: Audits operator queries and model calls; tracks pipeline lag, redaction failures and abstention rate.
data.service: IBM Cloud Activity Tracker / Cloud Monitoring

requirementDrafts.rationale: Uncited answers can mislead operators during an incident.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "an operator-facing answer with source evidence"
requirementDrafts.statement: Each incident explanation cites the log events and trace spans that support it, and abstains when evidence is insufficient.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prompt injection or leaked credentials in logs could compromise the analysis.
requirementDrafts.statement: Log and trace content is treated as untrusted data; instructions inside it are never followed, and secrets are redacted before storage or model calls.

requirementDrafts.rationale: watsonx.ai model availability varies by region; this decides placement.
requirementDrafts.basis: Open question; no country stated yet.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: logs, index and model processing stay in an agreed country; region not yet selected.

response.message: The emulation did finish its checks on design revision 2 without any failures. It reported blocked gaps instead: all eight components still need native IBM implementations, and the two existing systems still need a reference plan. That isn't something we got wrong in the design. Today's generator only has a narrow IBM contract for private object storage, and collection, redaction, OpenSearch, Code Engine and watsonx.ai still need to be built in the product, so I won't change or reduce the board to make the check pass. Nothing has been run against an IBM account, region or real model. Which country must the logs, the search index and the watsonx.ai processing stay in? That answer settles our region choice and which models we can use.
